title: Pose6DAug: Physically Plausible Multi-View Object Swapping for Robot Data Augmentation
claim: A policy fails on unseen objects; swapping the object in successful episodes via 3D pose and rendering yields fine-tuning data.
layout: 2 panels: left problem, right 5-step pipeline left-to-right, feedback arrows to policy
description: The figure has two rounded boxes. The left box, red-bordered and titled 'Problem: Object-Specific Failure', states that a policy trained on existing data may fail on an unseen object. It shows two real robot photos: a green 'Seen in Training ✓' one labeled success, and a red 'Target Object ×' one labeled failure. The task text reads 'Pick up the object and place it in the basket.' The right box, blue-bordered and titled 'Our Approach: Failure-Driven Object-Swap Augmentation', shows five numbered stages from left to right. Stage 1 retrieves stacked successful episode frames. Stage 2 shows gripper icons with pose axes at t0, t1 and tT, plus an 'Any6D + ICP' caption. Stage 3 swaps a dark box for a chocolate box with a down arrow. Stage 4 shows exo and ego camera frusta with rendered views. Stage 5 shows augmented multi-view video stacks. Black arrows from stages 1 and 5 feed a dashed 'Fine-tune VLA Policy' box at the bottom.
caption: Failure-driven object-swap augmentation. {(a)} Object-specific failure where a base policy fails to roll out plausible actions on an episode with novel object instances. {(b)} Given such failed episodes, we aim to synthesize physically plausible demonstrations for their object instances (target objects). We first retrieve successful demonstrations for the episodes with in-distribution object instances. Then, preserving their original action trajectory, we replace the manipulated objects with our target objects. Specifically, our method estimates a 3D mesh and a 6D pose sequence for a target object based on robot kinematics under a rigid coupling, which enables rendering physically plausible, multi-view consistent videos for fine-tuning the base policy.
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have shown strong potential for general-purpose manipulation, yet they often fail on novel, out-of-distribution objects whose appearance or geometry deviates from the training distribution. The standard remedy is to collect multi-view teleoperation data for every failure case, but this scales poorly in both cost and time. We introduce Pose6DAug, a failure-driven data augmentation framework that turns existing successful episodes into targeted demonstrations for a policy's failure modes, without any new data collection. Our key insight is that each successful episode already encodes a physically valid action trajectory together with calibrated multi-view observations. By swapping only the manipulated object while preserving this trajectory, we obtain new and physically grounded demonstrations. However, the challenge lies in synthesizing object swaps, e.g., naive 2D video editing breaks multi-view consistency and physical plausibility, particularly under heavy occlusion and egocentric viewpoints. Our method instead operates directly in 3D, anchoring the target object with an explicit mesh driven by a temporally coherent 6D pose trajectory. This ensures geometrically consistent renderings across all camera views. Fine-tuning a VLA on data augmented by our method improves success rates by 16.5% relative to the state-of-the-art baseline on novel objects, while preserving in-distribution performance. On a real robot, it more than doubles the success rate of the base policy. These results show that multi-view and physically consistent augmentation is a practical path to scalable VLA generalization.
